references.text: Describes the origin of the silver that came from the atonement money (a half shekel) that each Israelite had to pay during the census.
Continues the explanation about the silver and specifies that it came from the 603,550 men who were counted, each paying a beka (half shekel).
Confirms the total number of Israelite men (603,550) who were counted, which corresponds to the amount of silver collected.
Mentions the sanctuary shekel as the unit of measurement, the same standard used in Exodus 38:25.
Refers to the sanctuary shekel as the standard measure for valuation in the tabernacle service.
Describes how the silver was used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and for the hooks on the pillars.
The number in the source verse is the direct mathematical fulfillment of the rule established in this verse.
